written.text: Describe in detail how integers are stored in computer memory.
written.finalAnswer: Integers are stored as bits in memory. Unsigned whole numbers use all bits for the value, with maximum 2ⁿ − 1. Signed integers reserve the most significant bit as the sign bit, have maximum 2ⁿ⁻¹ − 1 and minimum −2ⁿ⁻¹, and store negative values using two's complement.

modelAnswer: Integers are stored in computer memory as bits; 1 byte has 8 bits.
An unsigned integer represents non-negative whole numbers and uses all its bits to store the value.
For n bits, the maximum unsigned value is 2ⁿ − 1.
For example, a 1-byte unsigned integer has a maximum value of 2⁸ − 1 = 255.
For signed integers, one bit is reserved as the sign bit, which is the most significant bit.
For n bits, the maximum signed value is 2ⁿ⁻¹ − 1 and the minimum is −2ⁿ⁻¹.
Negative values are stored using two's complement: invert all the bits and add 1.
For example, −5 in 8-bit two's complement is 11111011₂.

written.text: Explain the process of converting a decimal integer to its binary representation and vice versa. Include examples of both positive and negative integers.
written.finalAnswer: Positive integers can be written as sums of powers of 2. For example, 5₁₀ = 00000101₂. To represent −5 in 8-bit two's complement, invert 00000101₂ to get 11111010₂, then add 1 to get 11111011₂. For binary to decimal, add the place values of the 1 bits; 00000101₂ = 5₁₀, and 11111011₂ represents −5 in 8-bit two's complement.

modelAnswer: A positive decimal integer is written in binary using place values that are powers of 2.
For example, 5₁₀ = 00000101₂.
To convert binary to decimal, add the place values of the bits that are 1.
To represent −5, start with the binary representation of 5: 00000101₂.
Invert all the bits: 11111010₂.
So, −5 in 8-bit two's complement is 11111011₂.

explain.title: Whole numbers
explain.body: Whole numbers are a set of non-negative integers. They include zero and all the positive integers. Mathematically, the set of whole numbers is: W = {0,1,2,3...}. They suit quantities that cannot be negative, such as the number of students.

explain.title: Unsigned whole-number ranges
explain.body: A byte has 8 bits. For an unsigned whole number with n bits, the maximum value is 2ⁿ − 1. So, 1 byte has a maximum of 255, 2 bytes a maximum of 65,535, and 4 bytes a maximum of 4,294,967,295.

explain.title: Signed integers
explain.body: Integers extend the concept of whole numbers to include negative numbers. In computer programming, we call them signed integers. One bit is reserved as the sign bit (the most significant bit). For n bits, the maximum positive value is 2ⁿ⁻¹ − 1.

explain.title: Negative integers and two's complement
explain.body: To store negative values, computers use a method called two's complement. Invert all the bits, then add 1 to the Least Significant Bit (LSB). For 8-bit integers, the minimum is −2⁷ = −128.

mistakes: Do not confuse unsigned and signed ranges: an unsigned 1-byte number has maximum 255, while a signed 1-byte integer has maximum 127.
For a signed integer, remember that one bit is reserved as the sign bit.
Do not stop after inverting the bits when finding two's complement; you must add 1.
Keep the number of bits fixed in a two's-complement example, such as 8 bits.
Do not confuse the maximum signed value, 2ⁿ⁻¹ − 1, with the minimum, −2ⁿ⁻¹.
